sources: Early daguerreotype portraits (1839–1845) needed about 60–90 seconds of sitting still; after about 1845 (bromine) exposures fell to a few seconds; serious faces had other reasons too (photos were rare, expensive, solemn). Mental Floss, 'Daguerreotype Q&A'; Getty Museum (2023), 'Say Prunes! The surprising history of the smile in early photographs'.
Modern phone cameras in normal light: exposure times well under 1/100 s (general camera knowledge).
